name: Dowry

gist.Teocuilatl, the Embodiment of Gods: Tough hero who turns sacrifices into gold: an older creature for a little, or once per game one of her own heroes for a lot (which ends her turn).
gist.Willy, the Valiant Leprechaun: At the end of her first turn she takes either five cards or a pile of gold.
gist.Boris, the Guardian of Blackport: Her weapon carrier: sturdy, a fighter, and nothing she owns can be stolen or taken over.
gist.Wealth: Extra gold at the start of every turn, more per level.
gist.Golden Bananas: Three small gold gains in a row.
gist.Play Money: Makes the next artifact much cheaper.
gist.Vampiric Sword: Absurdly expensive sword: its hero heals for half of every attack's damage.
gist.The Sun Sword: More Attack, everything it hits is set on fire, and her side cannot be frozen.
gist.The Hands of Big Gwen: Costly equipment that adds Attack and a card-search rider on hits.
gist.Pocket Catapult: A small free shot at anything, every turn.
gist.Bamboo Shield: Pricey reaction that cancels one hit on a hero outright.
gist.Strong Shield: Reaction that cancels one very large hit.
gist.Golden Apple: Buys control of one of your heroes for a turn.
gist.Magic Ruby: Stuns one of your heroes for a turn; can be kept by discarding.
gist.Mimic: Small creature that steals gold from you every turn; also sacrifice fodder for Teocuilatl.

plan: Jessica out-spends you. Wealth, Willy's windfall, Treasure Chests and Mimics build a gold pile no other student has; it goes into jewellery for Boris (Sun Sword, Warhorse, eventually the Vampiric Sword) and into reactions that simply buy off your best hit. Boris then stuns with Heavy Hit, swings again with Quick Attack and heals off the damage, while Golden Apple borrows your own hero and Pocket Catapults nibble. It is a patient, well-defended deck with one obvious flaw: almost everything she paid for is equipment on a single hero, and her damage is one attack line that a freeze or a stun switches off.

looks.early: A heap of gold after turn one, a Mimic, Wealth on two heroes; nothing aggressive.
looks.mid: Boris glittering with a Sun Sword and a Warhorse, a Pocket Catapult on each side, gold in reserve for a shield.
looks.late: Boris with the Vampiric Sword healing back everything you do to him, and Jessica still holding enough gold to say no once more.

opening.tell: She took Willy's gold and is equipping, not attacking; a Mimic is taking a little of your gold each turn.
opening.why: She applies no pressure early and keeps gold ready to cancel exactly one big hit a turn, so racing wastes your best spells; use the calm to build the Storm, whose many small ticks her shields cannot buy off.

midgame.tell: Boris wears three pieces of equipment; her other two heroes wear none.
midgame.why: Fire Bomb destroys any number of equipped artifacts at once: one potion deletes everything she has paid for, while single big spells just walk into Bamboo Shield and Strong Shield.

crisis.tell: She has just emptied her purse for the Vampiric Sword; no gold is left on her side.
crisis.why: Her defence is bought turn by turn; in the one turn cycle after a huge purchase she cannot pay for a shield, and that is when direct damage finally lands.

endgame.tell: Boris has a Smug Coin, she has a Golden Ankh in hand and gold for one more Golden Apple.
endgame.why: Her last tricks each undo exactly one all-in turn, so keep Homerun! and your caster safe from the borrowed-hero turn and let repeated Storm ticks do what a single finisher cannot.
